content:
marta: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in fncall rejects since the strict-validator canary rolled out last night. Console shows a flood of `invalid_shape` but no field-level context. Anyone else?
liam: Yep, noticed it around 02:10 UTC. Affected a subset of customers in eu-west. Rate looks correlated with a bulk job that submits array of steps instead of object.
ankur: Confirmed on my end. Samples from logs: 
```
request.payload: {
  "steps": [ { "name": "extract", "args": [...] } ]
}
validator.error: invalid_shape: expected object at /steps
```
liam: The validator is rejecting at the top-level because schema expects `steps` to be an object keyed by id. Earlier permissive canary coerced arrays -> object; strict one removed coercion.
devex-nick: UX ask — we need the console to show a sampled request + the exact path that failed (e.g., `/steps/0/args`) and the model output that triggered it. Right now the dashboard just shows `invalid_shape` with counts.
ops-telemetry: Telemetry note: reject reasons are being aggregated to `reject.invalid_shape` but we don't index nested paths. We can start sending `reject.reason_path` as a tag but need to be careful with cardinality (user payload keys can explode). Proposal: emit up to 3 sampled distinct paths per minute and a hashed path tag for counts.
marta: Good idea. For immediate mitigation, can we route strict-validate failures to a permissive fallback pipeline (soft-validate) for enterprise customers while surfacing rejections for debugging? We should avoid user-facing 500s.
ankur: Routing policy discussion: fallback should be configurable per-customer (route_to: permissive|reject) and per-route. Also quota accounting — if we fallback and accept, do we bill at full generate cost or mark as diagnostic?
liam: Billing: keep billing consistent (incoming tokens billed). But mark telemetry with `validation_fallback=true` so we can track cost due to validation. Also we should exclude fallback traces from canary health metrics to avoid masking real failures.
devex-nick: Console UX: add a small “validation incidents” card on route/model page showing recent sampled payload + suggested schema patch (automated diff hint). Could display the minimal change to schema to accept the observed shape.
ops-telemetry: Implementation plan: 1) tag sampled failures with `path_hash`, `example_snippet` (redacted), `validation_mode`. 2) expose sample collector endpoint with retention 7d. 3) add an alert if sampled distinct paths > 50 in 5m (possible API break).
marta: Quick patch: revert strict-validator canary to run in `shadow` mode (log rejects but don't block) for the next deploy, while we roll a fallback config and telemetry tags. Who can flip it?
deploy-bot: Canary `strict-validate@v2` rollback scheduled by marta. Triggered rollback in 30s.
ankur: I'll open a tiny PR: routing flag `validation_policy: { mode: "enforce|shadow|fallback", fallback_target: "permissive" }` and telemetry fields. Will add tests for billing tags.
liam: Also add server-side sample redaction so PII isn't captured. Replace strings > 64 chars with `<<redacted>>`.
devex-nick: For the operator cookbook: include a checklist — detect spike, flip to shadow, enable fallback for impacted customers, collect 100 samples, propose schema patch, roll strict back to canary with alerts. I'll draft the doc after lunch. :memo:
marta: Thanks all — priority is avoiding customer errors. If you see unusual reject counts after rollback ping here. :thumbsup:
